The new dependency uses an exact version (`"1.95.1"`) while every other entry in `devDependencies` uses a caret range (`^x.y.z`). Pinning icons assets to an exact version is defensible for reproducibility, however this is inconsistent with the project's overall dependency-styling convention. Consider whether a caret range would be more appropriate here, or align other deps similarly if exact pinning is the new convention.

Also note: the script comment in `scripts/sync-lobe-icons.mjs` ("升级 lobehub 包版本后重跑一次即可") implies the package version is expected to be bumped occasionally when assets change. An exact pin is reasonable for that workflow, but worth a deliberate decision rather than an inconsistency.

comments.content: The 5 newly-added `Option` fields are initialized to `None` inline at the legacy migration site. Since the same 5-field pattern (`capabilities`/`temperature`/`top_p`/`max_tokens`/`system_prompt` all `None`) is now duplicated across 4 `ModelEntry` constructors in `schema.rs` (this file), `commands.rs` test helper, `keyring.rs` test helper, and `mod.rs` test helper — every future field addition requires touching all of them or the build breaks. Same simplification applies to the three test helpers, which currently have to be kept in lockstep with the struct shape.

comments.content: has_vendor_key is re-exported from this module but is missing from the bot.rs facade `pub use config::{...}` block (line 53–111). The module-level comment (line 6–8) explicitly states "所有外部调用走 `crate::bot::<item>`，不直接访问 `crate::bot::config::<item>`" — so external callers following that convention will not find has_vendor_key. Since it's only used internally by bot_get_config, this may be by design, but if so it should not be in the `pub use keyring::{...}` block at all (just `pub(crate) use`) to avoid misleading external callers into reaching the submodule path.

Substring-based assertions like `assert!(!clean.contains("temperature"))` could pass on the wrong serialization if some other field's value happened to contain that substring. With fields uniquely named in JSON the false-positive risk is small; this is more a robustness/style point than a real issue. Consider using parsed JSON (e.g. `serde_json::Value` and check `obj.get("temperature").is_none()`) for stronger guarantees.

`delete_vendor_key` is the only one of the four vendor CRUD ops that omits the `warn_fallback_once(KeySlot::Llm)` call. The plaintext branch here can delete a vendor key file on Linux without ever logging the per-process fallback notice — `read_vendor_key`, `has_vendor_key`, and `write_vendor_key` all warn first. If a user clears a vendor key on a headless Linux box they get no audit hint that the credential was just removed from a plaintext file, while every other vendor op will have logged the warning. Either add `warn_fallback_once(KeySlot::Llm)` before the `match key_backend()` block or extract a single `_vendor_op_with_warn` helper so all four paths stay in lock-step.

`read_llm_key` silently swallows any error from `read_vendor_key`, not just `NoEntry`. With System backend a keyring fault (locked keychain, permission denied) on the vendor path falls through to `read_api_key()` and the caller can never tell the difference between "vendor key not configured" and "vendor key unreadable — falling back to global key silently". Combined with the fact that `read_llm_key` is the hot path for `bot_chat`/`bot_model_loop`/`bot_plan`, this can mask real auth failures as successful LLM calls that hit the global key and may produce 401s from a different vendor's gateway. Suggest classifying the vendor result (NoEntry / OtherError / Ok-empty) and logging at least `OtherError` to `bot.log` before falling through, e.g. `if let Err(e) = read_vendor_key(&vendor) { if !matches!(e, CommandError::KeyringError(ref s) if s.starts_with("未配置")) { audit::audit_log(...); } }`.

`vendor_account("")` produces the keyring username `"vendor:"` and `vendor_plaintext_filename("")` produces `bot-api-key-vendor--<hash>.txt`. `active_vendor_of` filters empty vendors, but the public `read_vendor_key` / `write_vendor_key` / `delete_vendor_key` / `has_vendor_key` functions are reachable from `bot_clear_vendor_key` (`commands.rs:303`) without an empty check — only a `trim()`. A frontend bug or a malicious frontend (in dev/webview scripts) passing `vendor: ""` would silently create/delete the `vendor:` keyring account, potentially shadowing the global `api-key` lookup for any caller that gets routed through `vendor:`. Suggest rejecting empty/whitespace vendor at the keyring layer (return `Err(CommandError::InvalidArgument { field: "vendor".into(), reason: "...".into() })`) so the validation is enforced regardless of which Tauri command wrapper forgets to check. `bot_test_connection` (line 513–516) and `bot_set_config` (line 201–206) already filter empty, but `bot_clear_vendor_key` does not.

The new `vendor_key_tests` cover sanitization and `active_vendor_of` happy paths, but `read_llm_key` itself — the function that ties this whole module together for the bot hot path — has no coverage. The four cases worth asserting directly are: (1) active vendor has key → returns vendor key; (2) active vendor exists in list but its keyring read fails / key absent → falls back to `read_api_key()`; (3) active model present but its `vendor` field is empty → falls back; (4) `None` active_model_id → falls back. Today, the silent-error issue is masked by `if let Ok(k) = ...` and only an integration test would catch a regression. Suggest adding tests that drive `read_llm_key` against a tempdir-based plaintext backend with both a vendor file present and absent, plus a case where the vendor file is corrupt (not NotFound) to assert the current fall-through behaviour is intentional — at which point it can be reconsidered against the high-severity silent-swallow comment above.

`meta_model.provider_key` is used as a WHERE / JOIN column by `models_by_provider` and `JOINED_SELECT` (see `crate::meta::mod`), but no index is created here. After a full models.dev sync this table will hold thousands of rows, and every vendor-detail load will full-scan. Add `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_meta_model_provider ON meta_model(provider_key);`. (Note: `meta_provider.provider_key` is already the PRIMARY KEY so SQLite auto-indexes it, no extra index needed there.)

comments.content: TOCTOU race in `connection_test_unreachable_reports_error`: bind→drop→connect to the same port leaves a window where another process can rebind the port and make `probe_connection` see a real (non-error) response, turning the assertion `r.ok == false` flaky in CI under load. Either keep the listener bound without accepting (so the kernel queues SYN and reqwest returns a deterministic error) or pick a high reserved port that is guaranteed unused in the test harness.

Implicit dependency on `MockLlmServer::start()` returning a `base_url` that ends with `/v1`: both `connection_test_ok_on_2xx` and `connection_test_anthropic_format_same_path` assert `paths[0].contains("GET /v1/models")` while only passing `server.base_url` as-is, and `connection_test_anthropic_base_without_v1_gets_v1_prefix` derives the `/v1`-less base via `trim_end_matches("/v1")`. If the mock harness ever changes its base-URL layout (e.g., drops the `/v1` suffix to stay neutral), the first two tests will break with no clear diagnostic. Add an explicit assertion on the base-URL shape up front, or document the contract on `MockLlmServer::start()` so the coupling is intentional.

comments.content: [high] URL construction duplicates the very bug that `anthropic_messages_url` (bot_anthropic.rs) was JUST patched to fix in this same PR — it now strips `/v1/messages` and `/messages` suffixes before deciding where to append. `probe_connection` here does NOT do that stripping, so when the user pastes a full endpoint URL into Base URL (e.g. `https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic/messages` — exactly the case the anthropic_messages_url test `anthropic_messages_url("https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic/messages")` covers), the probe builds `https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic/messages/v1/models` and gets a guaranteed 404 on the user-facing 「测试连接」 button. Same issue on the openai branch when `base_url` ends with `/models`. Reuse the same suffix-stripping logic (or factor a tiny shared helper) so the two probes can't drift again.

[high] Inconsistent keyring error handling vs `bot_get_config` (which propagates `has_vendor_key(&v)?` at line 91). Here `.ok()` silently swallows `read_vendor_key` errors — a partial keyring backend outage (credential store locked / permission denied) during a test will make the probe silently fall back to the GLOBAL key and report a spurious 401/403 against the wrong credential. The same keyring failure is properly surfaced as `KeyringError` during config load. Either both should propagate, or both should fall back — the current asymmetry hides backend issues behind a misleading 「vendor X 鉴权失败」 UI.

comments.content: [medium] Undocumented edge case: when BOTH `incoming.models_by_provider` and `disk.models_by_provider` are `None`, `sig_sets` returns an empty map for both, so the `_ => false` arm drops EVERY vendor from `verified_vendors`. Likely intentional (「没有模型就没有可用性」), but surprising if a user ever saves with empty `models_by_provider` (schema migration writing a fresh file, future reset action, frontend bug sending empty state). Add a doc-comment line noting this behavior, and/or special-case the 「两都空」 situation to preserve the existing list.

[medium] `bot_test_connection` probe reads `read_vendor_key` OUTSIDE the config-file lock, then takes the lock via `update_config_file` to write `verified_vendors`. `bot_set_config` writes a new vendor key outside the lock (line 204) and then takes the same lock to call `prune_verified_vendors`. Sequence: (1) test probe reads K_old, (2) user saves → `bot_set_config` writes K_new + acquires lock + prunes vendor from verified_vendors (dropped because `key_overwritten == Some(v)`), (3) test probe completes successfully, (4) test's `update_config_file` acquires the lock + re-adds vendor. Final state: K_new in keyring, vendor in verified_vendors — but K_new was never tested. Tight mutex-serialized window but real. Snapshot the key under the same lock, or re-read the vendor key inside `update_config_file`'s closure.

[medium] `keyring::delete_vendor_key` runs BEFORE `super::io::update_config_file(&app, …)` and OUTSIDE the config-file lock. If the IPC handler is killed (or panics) between the keyring delete and the config write, the key is gone from the credential store but `verified_vendors` still lists the vendor — the UI shows a green dot until the next save, but the next test connection returns 401 and the user has no clear recovery path short of editing the config file. Same for the order in `bot_set_config` key-write → config-write (but that one already commits the in-memory `config` regardless). Either move the keyring delete into the `update_config_file` closure body (so key delete + verified_vendors update both happen under `lock_config_write`), or reverse the order (drop from verified first; if delete fails, re-add).

[low] `VendorKeyParam` is `pub` with only the parent-fn-level doc-comment; field-level docs and normalization contract are missing. `vendor` is used as a free-form keyring account name (`vendor:{vendor.trim()}`) and a free-form plaintext filename input. Frontend callers have no documented expectation: what trims do (already done at command boundary), what whitespace behavior is, whether Unicode/case is preserved (it is — see keyring.rs vendor_plaintext_filename, which case-folds into filenames). Add `///` on each field stating trim/case/Unicode behavior and the max-length bounds (none today, but should match `MAX_KEYWORD` or similar).

[low] `sig_sets` inside `prune_verified_vendors` uses fully-qualified `std::collections::BTreeMap` / `BTreeSet` paths repeated inside a nested `fn` (commands.rs:152-171). Hoist a `use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};` to the test-module or top of file. Functionally fine, but this is the most complex part of the new module and the FQN noise hurts readability.

Test concurrency hazard: `apply_sync_writes_and_reupdates` (sync test, in-memory DB) and `sync_with_bad_url_returns_err` (`#[tokio::test]`) both ultimately call `apply_sync`, which acquires `crate::db::lock_db_write()` — a process-wide `DB_WRITE_LOCK` Mutex (see db/mod.rs:332). Under cargo's default parallel test runner, these two tests will serialize on that global lock and any other test in the suite touching `lock_db_write` will queue behind them. Consider either (a) `#[serial_test::serial]` on tests that touch the global lock, (b) running these two specific tests in a dedicated `#[cfg(test)]` module that takes a per-test local lock instead of `lock_db_write()`, or (c) documenting that meta sync tests must run single-threaded (`cargo test -- --test-threads=1`).

`sync_models_dev_with_url` is declared `pub` and accepts an arbitrary `url: &str`; the doc comment explicitly says "URL 可注入" for testability, but `pub` visibility means it is reachable from anywhere inside the crate (and externally, if `meta` is ever exposed as a library surface). Although the only currently-registered Tauri command (`meta_sync_models_dev`, meta/mod.rs:513) takes no URL and hardcodes `MODELS_DEV_API`, this seam should be `pub(crate)` (tests still see it via `use super::*;`) so a future accidental `#[tauri::command]` registration does not turn it into an SSRF vector letting the frontend fetch arbitrary URLs (127.0.0.1, cloud metadata endpoints, etc.) and pipe the response into `parse_models_dev` → `apply_sync`.

`fetch_models_dev` reuses `crate::bot_model_loop::shared_llm_client()` (bot_model_loop.rs:399, `OnceLock<reqwest::Client>`), which is the same connection pool used by every LLM call in `bot_chat`/`bot_plan`/`bot_model_loop`. Reusing the pool is the right call for connection-reuse, but: (1) the shared client has no special headers, but reqwest still attaches a default `User-Agent` that identifies the app — metadata fetches will then leak this UA to models.dev with every sync; (2) the pool is now contended by metadata sync and active LLM sessions — a sync that takes the full 30s timeout will queue behind in-flight LLM requests on the same pool. Either (a) attach a metadata-specific default User-Agent via a thin wrapper client, or (b) document explicitly that this client is now multi-purpose and that pool contention is acceptable.

`MetaModel.context_length` is `Option<i64>` (meta/mod.rs:41), but the parsed value is unbounded — `as_i64` silently accepts negative numbers (a buggy/hostile payload saying `"context": -1` would store `-1` and break any UI/consumer that assumes non-negative) and silently drops JSON floats and values >`i64::MAX`. Guard explicitly: `as_i64().filter(|n| *n >= 0)` so downstream code can rely on `>= 0`.

comments.content: Startup spawn fires on every app launch with no freshness check or rate limit. A user who restarts the app multiple times will hammer models.dev each time. Consider adding a "last-synced" timestamp check (e.g. only sync if older than N hours, similar to memory::consolidate's last_run_at gate) to be polite to the upstream API and reduce unnecessary cold-start latency.

Order of operations risk: `keyring::delete_vendor_key` runs BEFORE `update_config_file`. If the disk write fails (disk full, IO error, config file lock contention), the key is gone from keyring but `verified_vendors` still lists the vendor — UI keeps showing green plug while the key has actually been cleared, and next bot_set_config with the same vendor name would silently re-fail verify. Prefer to mutate `verified_vendors` first, then delete the key (or wrap both under CONFIG_WRITE_LOCK + keyring delete as a single transaction-like sequence, mirroring how `bot_set_config` already does key-then-config with the comment "先后半成功问题已转 B 类评估").

Silent verified_vendors write failure: if `update_config_file` fails, the error is only `eprintln!`'d. The user sees a successful test (UI goes green), but on next app launch the vendor is back to unverified (or stays green-but-stale until next bot_set_config prunes it). At minimum, surface the failure to the result or audit it structurally — UI expects the green state to be persisted, not best-effort. The current contract "写盘失败不阻断测试结果的返回" hides a real persistence bug from the user.

Vendor key read swallows real keyring errors: `.ok()` on `read_vendor_key(v)` discards any `Err` (locked keychain, permission denied, backend unavailable) and silently falls through to the global key or empty string. The doc comment says "不主动把 keyring 故障伪装成连接失败", but the practical effect is the opposite — vendor lockout / locked-keychain bug is reported to the user as "401 unauthorized, check your API key" when the real issue is on the user's local keychain. The frontend will then persist a false `verified_vendors` entry removal (line 528-530) on a healthy vendor that just couldn't be read with the vendor-scoped key. Match the strategy used by `bot_get_config` for `has_api_key` — let real keyring errors propagate as `CommandError::KeyringError` so the frontend can prompt the user to unlock keychain.

comments.content: Empty vendor string is not short-circuited: `bot_clear_vendor_key("", "")` would still call `delete_vendor_key("")` which constructs `keyring::Entry::new(KEYRING_SERVICE, "vendor:")` (empty vendor name after the prefix). On the Linux plaintext fallback, the file becomes `bot-api-key-vendor--811c9dc5.txt` (visible to the user in their data dir). Add `if vendor.is_empty() return Ok(())` at the top, mirroring the `bot_set_config` pattern of skipping empty vendor writes.

Long-running transaction under DB_WRITE_LOCK: `apply_sync` wraps the entire provider+model upsert loop in one transaction AND holds `db::lock_db_write()` for the whole duration. With models.dev typically returning 200+ providers and 1000+ models, that's 1000+ SQL UPDATEs under a single write lock. Concurrent paths (memory consolidate every 10min, persist_last_run on every bot_chat turn, MCP server edits, etc.) will be fully blocked until the sync finishes — usually fast but a 5-second timeout means worst-case 5s of UI write stalls. Consider chunking: commit every N upserts, or use INSERT OR REPLACE with a smaller per-statement transaction. The "all or nothing" transactional guarantee doesn't add value for cached sync data.

Manual `meta_sync_models_dev` returns `MetaSyncResult` directly (not `CommandResult<MetaSyncResult>`). A panic inside the closure (e.g. a SQL edge case, malformed models.dev response) would propagate uncaught and abort the IPC handler, killing the JS-side promise with a generic "command panicked" error instead of a recoverable `ok:false` shape that the UI knows how to render. Wrap the body in a panic catch or convert panic → `MetaSyncResult { ok: false, error: ... }` via `std::panic::catch_unwind` for the user's manual "更新模型库" button. The startup spawn already silently handles errors via audit; manual UI calls deserve the same UX.

Inconsistent serialization contract with sibling types: `BotConfigView` uses `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` (verified at types.rs:339), but `MetaProvider` / `MetaModel` / `MetaModelJoined` (meta/mod.rs:23,36,51) have no `rename_all`. Frontend `src/lib/modelMeta.ts:8-30` is forced to use snake_case fields (`provider_key`, `provider_name`, `display_name`, `context_length`, etc.) — different from the rest of the codebase. Pick one direction and apply uniformly: either add `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` to the meta structs and update the TS types, OR document the deliberate snake_case choice as a module-level invariant. Inconsistency here is a future-trap: the next contributor adding a single-word field to `BotConfigView` will be surprised by the asymmetry.

if (model.topP !== undefined && (n <= 0 || n > 1)) return;
if (model.maxTokens !== undefined && n < 1) return;

或 at least 把无效分支在 UI 上反馈（红框/aria-invalid），让用户知道为什么没保存。

comments.content: `onTested?.()` 在 invoke 抛异常分支也被调用。后端只有 `if let Some(v) = vendor` 的两个分支（push/retain）真正修改盘上的 `verified_vendors`；invoke 异常时（panic / Tauri runtime 错误）这两个分支都没跑，parent 又走一次 `loadConfig()` 反而会把内存里的 `verified_vendors` 用未变化的盘上值重写一遍（虽然多数情况下两者一致），徒增 IO 与抖动。建议只在 try 块正常结束（含 ok=false 的受控失败）时调 `onTested?.()`，catch 分支仅保留错误展示、不通知父级（或延迟到下一次 `bot-config-changed`）。

数字 input 的 onBlur 在 `Number.isFinite(n)` 失败时（用户输入非数字如 `abc`）静默无操作，DOM 仍保留 `abc` 字符串，state 也没改。提示与 temperature/topP/maxTokens 的约束（已在 confirmed #4 中提及）属于「前端基本校验」，建议至少在解析失败时给本地 testMsg 之类的反馈（或者保持焦点、不让用户离开），否则用户以为已落盘但实际没有。

MetaSyncResult uses a loose boolean flag plus optional members, which permits payloads such as { ok: true, providers: undefined, models: undefined } or { ok: false, providers: 5, error: '...' } at the type level. Consumers (SettingsPage) will then hit runtime undefineds when reading providers/models on success. Use a discriminated union keyed on ok so TypeScript narrows the shape and the call site is forced to handle success/failure correctly.

All three catch arms swallow the underlying error without any logging (no console.error, no telemetry hook). When meta_list_providers/meta_models_by_provider/meta_sync_models_dev start failing in production there will be no signal to debug from. Since the design intent is to downgrade silently on the UX side, at minimum mirror the error to console so it can still be observed in DevTools without changing the return contract.

`build.assetsInlineLimit` is a build-time Vite option that controls the output of `vite build` (and `vitest build`), not Vite's dev server / module graph that Vitest uses during test runs (`vitest run`, `vitest`, `vitest --ui`, `vitest run --coverage` in package.json). Since none of the test scripts invoke `vitest build`, this entire `build` block is effectively dead config and the comment's claim that "测试里也走文件路径" is misleading.

Two things actually already ensure the test sees URL paths, not data URIs:
1. `import.meta.glob("../../assets/providers/lobe/*.svg", { query: "?url", import: "default" })` in `providerLogoMap.ts` forces URL handling for every SVG at the module level, independent of size — so `assetsInlineLimit` is a no-op for this code path even in a real build.
2. The test helper `expectLogoSlug` (SettingsPage.test.tsx:10) explicitly handles both `data:` URIs and `lobe/<slug>` paths.

Either drop this `build` block from `vitest.config.ts` (keep it only in `vite.config.ts` where it actually applies to the production bundle), or rewrite the comment to reflect what it really does (nothing observable in tests).

Confirmed #6 (low): `VendorKeyParam` has no field-level docs. The struct's two fields are used in three different roles — as a keyring account name (`vendor:{vendor.trim()}`), as a free-form plaintext filename input (sanitized via FNV-1a hash suffix in keyring.rs), and as a free-form verified-vendors identifier. Trim is performed at the call site before write/delete, but readers (`bot_get_config`, `bot_test_connection`) also defensively re-trim before using. Add a short comment documenting: (a) trim semantics (caller-responsible), (b) the relationship between `vendor` here and `ModelEntry.vendor` (must match exactly to be valid), (c) the empty-vendor behavior (silently ignored).

Compound-suffix normalization is order-dependent and incomplete: the paren regex `/\s*[（(][^)）]*[)）]\s*$/` is anchored to `$`, so it only matches when a parenthetical group is the LAST thing in the string. If a models.dev display name has a parenthetical BEFORE a plan suffix — e.g., `"Alibaba (China) Token Plan"` — the paren regex does not match (string ends with `plan`), then the plan-suffix regex strips ` token plan`, leaving `"alibaba (china)"`. The remaining paren then causes `resolveLobeIcon` alias lookup to miss, AND in SettingsPage.tsx (lines 899-908) the preset / meta match `normalizeVendorName(p.provider_name) === norm` fails, so the provider cannot be located even when the user-typed vendor name normalizes correctly. Suggested fix: apply the two replaces in a loop until stable, or use a single regex like `/(\s*[（(][^)）]*[)）]\s*|\s+(token plan|coding plan|step plan))+$/` to consume any combination of trailing paren groups and plan suffixes in one pass.
